exposure: Maternal age (teenage primigravidae aged 15-19 years vs. adult primigravidae aged 20-29 years)
outcome: Antenatal complications (anemia, pre-term labor, pregnancy-induced hypertension)
Neonatal morbidity (birth asphyxia, NICU admissions, hyperbilirubinemia)
cohort: The study included 80 teenage primigravidae (15-19 years) and 160 adult primigravidae (20-29 years) from a hospital setting.
finding: Teenage primigravidae experienced significantly higher rates of antenatal complications, lower hemoglobin levels, increased cesarean section rates, more pre-term births, higher incidence of low birth weight babies, and greater neonatal morbidity compared to adult primigravidae.
mod_finding: Teenage mothers had a significantly higher cesarean section rate (45%) compared to adult mothers (20.6%), with fetal distress being the main indication.
